I'm looking for a maximal triangle-free graph on 8 vertices that includes edges (0,6) and (2,6). The key insight is that a complete bipartite graph like K_{4,4} is both triangle-free and maximal, so I can partition the vertices strategically—placing 0 and 2 on one side with 6 on the other to satisfy the required edges.

Setting A={0,2,4,5} and B={1,3,6,7}, I connect every vertex in A to every vertex in B, giving me 16 edges total. This construction guarantees no triangles exist (since any three vertices must include at least two from the same part, which aren't connected), and it's maximal because adding any edge within a part would immediately create a triangle through any vertex in the opposite part.
